newsitem.title: USA: Floods cut Thai rice crop to 14.4 MMT-US attache.
newsitem.headline: Floods cut Thai rice crop to 14.4 MMT-US attache.

text.p: Thailand's rice crop will be smaller than expected -- 13.86 million tonnes -- due to flood damage, the U.S. agricultural attache in Bangkok said in a report released Monday.
Exports were still forecast for five million tonnes, which would allow a slight rebuilding of stocks, the attache said.

The attache pegged this year's rice crop at 21 million tonnes paddy basis and 13.86 million tonnes milled basis. Earlier, the crop was estimated at 21.38 million tonnes paddy basis and 14.39 million tonnes milled.
In early February, USDA estimated the Thai rice crop at 14.40 million tonnes with exports of 5.5 million tonnes.

"Post's forecast of Thailand's 1996/97 rice crop is revised downward to 21.0 million metric tons (paddy basis) as a lower than normal yield resulted in the main crop coming in below previous expectations (16.2 mmt vs. 18.0 mmt)," the attache wrote.
"The reduction was partially offset by a larger than expected second crop, which is now forecast at 4.8 mmt, due to increased area and wider use of high-yielding varieties.

"Based on a recent survey on the 1996/97 main crop in the Central Plains, we found that paddy fields in certain areas suffered more flood damage than earlier expected, although less than the previous year."
